item.title: Svajda: Grief, gratitude and a homecoming triumph in memory of his father
item.description: After spending just four days in Asia last September, far short of his planned three-week stay, Zachary Svajda returned home to California. The American played one qualifying match at the ATP 250 event in Chengdu and admittedly struggled to focus in that defeat, even breaking down in tears before the match. item.title: Alcaraz rallies past Khachanov in Doha, hits perfect 10 for 2026
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz prevailed in a Doha tussle on Thursday at the Qatar ExxonMobil Open to preserve his perfect start to 2026. The No. 1 player in the PIF ATP Rankings overcame Karen Khachanov 6-7(1), 6-4, 6-3 to seal his semi-final spot at the hard-court ATP 500. item.title: Mensik stuns Sinner in Doha for biggest win of his career
item.description: Jakub Mensik has pedigree when it comes to causing upsets at the Qatar ExxonMobil Open. Yet the 20-year-old hit new heights at the ATP 500 on Thursday, when he stunned World No. 2 Jannik Sinner with a classy quarter-final performance. Mensik upset Sinner 7-6(3), 2-6, 6-3 for the biggest win of his career by PIF ATP Ranking. item.title: Play in Rio de Janeiro resumes following rain delay
item.description: Thursday's Play has resumed at the Rio Open presented by Claro after a second rain delay. Following about an hour-long wait, Joao Fonseca will play Ignacio Buse on Quadra Guga Kuerten. Matteo Berrettini vs. Dusan Lajovic was scheduled to follow but was moved to Quadra 1. The first delay happened for approximately 45 minutes when Tomas Martin Etcheverry was three points from victory against Vilius Gaubas at 7-6(1), 5-3 15/15. item.title: Putting Sinner's Doha defeat in perspective: The numbers behind his consistency
item.description: Losses have been rare for Jannik Sinner in recent years. That is why when the Italian does fall short, it grabs plenty of people's attention. item.title: Buse upsets Fonseca in Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Ignacio Buse spoiled Joao Fonseca’s pursuit of home glory at the Rio Open presented by Claro on Thursday when he upset the Brazilian 5-7, 6-3, 6-4 in the second round. Despite losing the first set in the pair's maiden Lexus ATP Head2Head meeting, Buse eventually capitalised on Fonseca’s 43 unforced errors to triumph in a two-hour, 26-minute battle. item.title: Tien rallies to shock defending champ in Delray Beach: 'I just kept believing'
item.description: Learner Tien was not ready for his Delray Beach Open to come to an end.
